QF.id: AIFM CIII AIFs in India and Suitability_3

question.text: Aravalli Long-Short Fund (a Category III AIF) has investible funds of INR 500 crore. The risk officer Ms. Priya Shah is reviewing the maximum permissible exposure to a single investee company. Per SEBI (AIF) Regulations, what is the cap?

answer.text: INR 125 crore, being 25% of investible funds (same as Category II AIF)
INR 50 crore, being 10% of investible funds
INR 25 crore, being 5% of investible funds
No cap, since Category III AIFs employ complex strategies including leverage

explanation.text: The Logic: Table 4.1 specifies the Cat III single-investee concentration cap as 10% of investible funds of the AIF scheme. On INR 500 crore investible funds, that is INR 50 crore. This is tighter than Cat I/II's 25% cap, reflecting the higher-leverage nature of Cat III portfolios. The Trap: Option A swaps in the Cat I/II 25% cap — a classic cross-category trap. Option C invents a 5% cap. Option D is wrong: Cat III has complex strategies but concentration is MORE constrained, not uncapped. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-D (Cat I/II Manager) tests 25% concentration with Angel Fund carve-outs (INR 10 lakh - INR 25 crore). XIX-E tests the tighter 10% cap for Cat III. Manager's Pro-Tip: When sizing a single-name stat-arb or pair-trade position, remember the 10% cap is on the INVESTEE LEVEL — gross long and short legs against the same issuer count. SEBI's interpretation is strict; build a pre-trade compliance screen so your prime broker doesn't execute breaches.
